# temps_dns_provider (Resource)

A DNS host Temps creates records in (certificate challenges, generated hostnames). Hand it zones with `temps_dns_provider_domain`.

Import with `<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `dns_providers:read`, `dns_providers:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_dns_provider" "cloudflare" {
  name          = "Cloudflare"
  provider_type = "cloudflare"
  credentials   = jsonencode({ api_token = var.cloudflare_token })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `credentials` (String, Sensitive) Credentials for `provider_type`, for example `jsonencode({ api_token = var.cloudflare_token })` for Cloudflare. The `type` key is filled in from `provider_type`. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.
- `name` (String) Name of the provider.
- `provider_type` (String) DNS host. One of `azure`, `bunny`, `cloudflare`, `digitalocean`, `gcp`, `namecheap`, `pebble`, `route53`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the provider is for.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether Temps uses the provider.

### Read-Only

- `flat_hostnames_supported` (Boolean) Whether the provider can serve generated hostnames one level below the zone.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `<id>`.
- `last_error` (String) Last error the provider returned.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id>
terraform import temps_dns_provider.cloudflare 1
```
